name: AHT30 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Aosong (ASAIR) digital temperature (-40 to 85 °C on the module, ±0.3–0.5 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2–3 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface and a CRC-checked 20-bit reading; no calibration command needed. The module has a 3.3 V regulator, 4.7 kΩ I2C pull-ups and a MOSFET level shifter. Sold as: purple AHT30 temperature & humidity sensor module (GY-style, 4-pin 2.54 mm header: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA), fixed I2C address 0x38.
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply to the module's 3.3 V regulator, 2.5–5.5 V; use your board's logic voltage (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico) because the SDA/SCL pull-ups on the host side go to VIN

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the module)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the module)

supplierQuery: AHT30 temperature humidity sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Header order printed on the module: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA.
Power VIN from the microcontroller's logic voltage (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico): the board's level shifter pulls the host-side SDA/SCL up to VIN, so 5 V on VIN would put 5 V on a 3.3 V board's I2C pins.
The module already has 4.7 kΩ pull-ups on SDA and SCL; no extra resistors are needed.
Wait at least 5 ms after power-on, then measure: send 0xAC 0x33 0x00, wait 80 ms, read 7 bytes (status, 20-bit humidity, 20-bit temperature, CRC). Status bit 7 set means still busy: read again.
Check the CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF over the first 6 bytes). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Measure no more than once a second (the datasheet's limit for under 0.1 °C self-heating) and keep the sensor away from the regulator and the microcontroller.
The address is fixed at 0x38, so only one AHT30 (or AHT10/20/21) per I2C bus.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from aht30 import AHT30

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = AHT30(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(2)
